admission_apply.text: You press the short seam. It yields no note. The miss leaves that edge and appears on the next.

native.admission_inspect: A palm-square of pale horn, thinner than a card. Three edges match. The fourth is short, and the plate gives no hum.
apply_texts: Measure and thumb disagree by the same hair. You press. The error changes side and remains that large.
Opposite you, the seam fails by a hair. You press. The failure slides, and the plate stays silent.
The left edge is the short one now. Flat pressure moves the miss onward. Still no hum in the horn.
The mute plane steadies the count. The short edge shifts one place and stays smaller than the doubt.
The short seam will not travel. Pressure leaves the same three true edges and one that fails them.
You press the short seam. It yields no note. The miss leaves that edge and appears on the next.
inspect_texts: A palm-square of pale horn, thinner than a card. Three edges match. The fourth is short, and the plate gives no hum.
Pale horn, still mute. The short edge has moved to the left. The other three agree, and none explains the miss.
Sight calls the sides equal. A closer span finds the fourth short by less than a breath. The plate has no depth to spare.
The far edge is the short one. Three sides match. The plate is flat enough to shame the discrepancy, and it will not hum.
The square will not sit as one plane. A ridge meets the thumb where no edge is drawn. Counting does not close.
Under the thumb the near edge stops early. The square shows one face only. The miss is smaller than any name for it.
native.name: Short-Seam Square
